**PASS+NOTES** ## What I ran - Read both `result.json` files and diffed the base→head change (`git diff c6c8c5e..b9e745d`, 14 files: `usage.ts`, client `model/message/update/subscription/index`, `factory.stylex.ts`, `usage.test.ts`, `verify.mjs`, skill docs, `traces-pass.json` fixture). - Unpacked three head traces (`seeded-1280-light`, `seeded-1280-dark`, `seeded-390-light`, plus `empty-1280-light` and `sparse-1280-light`), parsed `trace.trace` action/snapshot/screencast events, and viewed the actual screencast JPEGs of the usage page in light, dark, and 390 — not just status fields. - Adversarial probe in `/tmp/verifier-break` (bash only, no install/server/browser): copied `fixture.json`, corrupted `generatedAt` to `not-a-date` / `""` and stretched it 10 minutes into the future, then exercised the exact arithmetic and date semantics the new `updatedText` in `apps/web/src/features/usage.ts` relies on. ## Base vs head - **Base (c6c8c5e)**: the run stops after 4 passing actions (doctor, factory-layout, factory-entry, usage-entry) and times out at the `usage-updated` wait for `Updated HH:MM (N min ago)`. This is the red/green before-state — the driver (identical skill files on both sides, md5-verified) requires the new feature. The base failure screenshot confirms it: no age line under "Usage", and only OpenCode and Vercel Token Pass headings are links (the old `Partial` `planHrefs`); Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, OpenRouter, CommandCode are plain text. - **Head (b9e745d)**: all 14 cases passed with 0 errors, covering all 44 selected journeys. Screenshots and ARIA/DOM snapshots show the feature working: - **usage-updated**: `Updated 00:41 (15114 min ago)` (15115 on the later 390 run) under the Usage title in light 1280, dark 1280, and light 390, consistent with the fixture's `2026-11-15T00:41:07Z` and the wall clock; the driver additionally asserts the printed minutes match `Date.now()`-derived elapsed within ±1, and it passed. - **usage-cards**: all seven headings render as links with the `↗` cue (`aria-label "Open X usage page"`, `target=_blank`, `rel=noopener`, correct href per plan), hover underline verified via computed style in the trace, heading order matches the fixture's heaviest-first order. - **usage-details**: Windows disclosures expand inside their own cards (Weekly 67%, month 100%) with the age line still present. - **usage-empty / usage-no-plans**: "No usage numbers yet." (no feed, no age line) and "No plans yet." render correctly. - Everything else (factory, kpis, shipping, home/reports/explorations hub, items 404/400/HEAD, share auth/validate/publish/delete, not-found, verifier-selection) passed; `traces.json` maps every browser journey to its trace, and untraced journeys are explained: access-anonymous's live probe answered 302 to the Cloudflare Access login URL, share journeys are request-context driven, verifier-selection recorded all 5 expected==actual picker results. - Install/build logs are clean; dev logs end only with the expected SIGTERM shutdown; `worktree.patch` is empty (checkouts clean). ## Adversarial findings - `feed.ts` declares `generatedAt: Schema.String`, so a corrupted feed with a garbage date still parses — the cards keep rendering, and the new age line silently disappears (`DateTime.make` → `Option.none` → no `

`), rather than crashing or printing junk. Graceful degradation, verified against the code path and the unit tests (`expectElement(text(/^Updated /u)).not.toExist()` before the first tick). - Boundary arithmetic: +59s → `0 min ago`, +90s → `1 min ago` (floors, never rounds up); a future-dated feed clamps to `0 min ago` via `Math.max(0, …)` — never a negative age. ## Notes for the reviewer 1. The age line is client-side only (`nowMs` arrives via the 30-second `TickedClock` subscription); the server-rendered HTML has no age line, so a first paint or no-JS fetch of `/usage` shows cards without it. By design, but worth knowing. 2. The sparse fixture keeps `generatedAt`, so the "No plans yet." page also shows the age line — consistent (data exists → show its age), just not mentioned in the sparse journey's phrasing. 3. `Math.max(0, …)` means a skewed/future feed timestamp reads as "0 min ago" (looks fresh) instead of flagging the skew; acceptable, nothing negative is ever printed. 4. With the run clock ~10.5 days past the fixture date, the line printed 5-digit minute counts (`15114 min ago`); the driver regex and layout handle it.
